name: All Fours (Trinidad)
description: All Fours, colloquially known as 'All Foes', is the national card game of Trinidad and Tobago. It is a highly competitive, anti-clockwise partnership game where 'hanging the Jack' (capturing the opponent's Jack) is considered the ultimate tactical victory.

overview.description: All Fours, colloquially known as 'All Foes', is the national card game of Trinidad and Tobago. It is a highly competitive, anti-clockwise partnership game where 'hanging the Jack' (capturing the opponent's Jack) is considered the ultimate tactical victory.

history.origins: Brought to the Caribbean by English colonial administrators, the game took deep root in Trinidadian culture, evolving from a simple tavern game into a sophisticated sport with national tournaments.
timeline: 1800s: Traditional English All Fours is introduced to Trinidad.
Early 1900s: Rules shift to an anti-clockwise direction and a 14-point target.
Present: A central part of social life, played in community centers and sanctioned leagues across the island.
history.cultural: All Fours in Trinidad is noted for its high-tension atmosphere and loud, physical card-playing style (often 'slamming' cards for emphasis).
history.evolution: The most significant Caribbean innovations were the 'Hang Jack' bonus (3 points) and the immediate scoring of turn-up cards (Ace, Six, Jack).

setup.dealing: Deal and play are STRICTLY anti-clockwise. Each player receives 6 cards (usually dealt 3 at a time). The 25th card is turned up for trumps.

rules.objective: Be first to 14 or more points by combining turn-up bonuses with High, Low, Jack, and Game.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Trump Bonus**: If the turned-up card is an Ace (1 pt), Six (2 pts), or Jack (3 pts), the dealer's team scores immediately. 2. **The Beg**: The player to the dealer's right (Eldest) chooses to 'Stand' or 'Beg'. 3. **The Gift/Run**: If they beg, dealer can gift 1 point to opponents or 'Run the cards' (deal 3 more and flip new trump). Score again for new A/6/J. 4. **Trick Play**: Follow suit or trump. 5. **Counting Out**: Points are scored in order: High, Low, Jack, Game.
keyRules: High (1 pt): Team dealt the highest trump.
Low (1 pt): Team dealt the lowest trump.
Jack (1 pt): Winning a trick with the Jack of trumps.
Hang Jack (3 pts): Winning a trick containing an opponent's Jack of trumps.
Game (1 pt): Team with most card pips (A=4, K=3, Q=2, J=1, 10=10).
Direction: Dealing, play, and turn-order are all anti-clockwise.

strategy.basic: Prioritize capturing the 10s of any suit; they are the fastest way to win the 'Game' point.
strategy.intermediate: The Lead: If your partner has the High trump (Ace), lead a small trump to 'pull' the opponent's trumps and expose their Jack.
strategy.advanced: Hanging the Jack: High-level play revolves around detecting who holds the Jack. If you suspect an opponent has a 'lone' Jack, lead an Ace of trumps immediately to 'Hang' it for 3 points.
tips: Never lead the Jack unless you are 100% sure it will win. It's a 3-point liability.
The 6 of trumps is a key swing card because it can score as a turn-up bonus and still matter in trick control.

scoring.winCondition: First team to reach 14 or more points wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Experience the intense, anti-clockwise battle of 'All Foes'. Hunt the Jack for 3 points, score bonuses on the flip, and reach 14 to become the island champion.
